title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 95
paragraphs: There appeared among the Medes a man of great ability whose name was Deioces, and this man was the son of Phraortes. This Deioces, having formed a desire for despotic power, did this: whereas the Medes dwelt in separate villages, he, being even before this time of great repute in his own village, set himself to practice just dealing much more and with greater zeal than before. And this he did although there was much lawlessness throughout the whole of Media, and although he knew that injustice is ever at feud with justice. The Medes of his own village, seeing his ways, chose him for their judge. So Deioces, since he was aiming at power, was upright and just; and doing thus he received no small praise from his fellow citizens, so that those of the other villages, learning that Deioces was a man who, more than any other, gave decisions rightly—whereas before this they had been accustomed to suffer from unjust judgments—they too, when they heard it, came gladly to Deioces to have their causes determined. At last they entrusted the business to no one else.
